stages.name: Junior Engineer
stages.summary: Delivers bounded work with clear goals and guidance, understands the intended result, verifies outputs, and learns actively.

business-results.text: Clarifies the user, goal, and acceptance conditions before starting a task.
business-results.evidence: Can restate the user, intended change, and completion conditions.

business-results.text: Completes agreed work and promptly surfaces deviations that could affect the result.
business-results.evidence: Deliverable meets the agreement; risks or delays are raised early.

business-results.text: Uses AI to accelerate low-risk work and checks facts, code, and references before submitting.
business-results.evidence: Can explain the change and show execution or manual review evidence.

domain-expertise.text: Applies foundational role knowledge to common tasks and asks for help when uncertain.
domain-expertise.evidence: Work passes basic checks and key concepts can be explained.

domain-expertise.text: Follows team quality, security, and privacy practices and checks edge cases before submission.
domain-expertise.evidence: Can identify obvious failure paths or sensitive-data risks.

domain-expertise.text: Provides useful context to AI and judges whether its output fits the task.
domain-expertise.evidence: Changes include verification; generated content is not assumed correct.

team-influence.text: Communicates progress, blockers, and needed support clearly.
team-influence.evidence: Collaborators know the status in time to act.

team-influence.text: Uses review feedback to improve the work.
team-influence.evidence: Can explain why feedback was adopted or discussed.

team-influence.text: Works within role and authorization boundaries and escalates decisions beyond them.
team-influence.evidence: Does not make unauthorized commitments affecting others or users.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Turns feedback into a concrete improvement in the next task.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Fewer repeat issues or reuse of a new method on a related task.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Separates known facts, hypotheses, and unknowns when describing a problem.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: States what observations support a view and what remains unverified.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Represents contributions, mistakes, and risks honestly and closes owned work.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Corrects the record promptly and does not conceal issues or overstate results.

stages.name: Mid-level Engineer
stages.summary: Independently owns a defined feature or component and delivers user and business outcomes with dependable quality.

business-results.text: Owns delivery of a feature and tracks whether it solves the intended user problem.
business-results.evidence: Reviews adoption, completion, or user feedback after release and adjusts.

business-results.text: Makes evidence-based trade-offs among cost, quality, and speed within agreed goals.
business-results.evidence: Explains the choice, alternatives, and conditions that could change the result.

business-results.text: Uses AI in controlled parts of the workflow to improve throughput while owning the user outcome.
business-results.evidence: Compares workflow time or quality and retains human review points.

domain-expertise.text: Designs a maintainable component solution and identifies interfaces, state, and major failure modes.
domain-expertise.evidence: Design supports requirements and explains capacity, migration, or rollback.

domain-expertise.text: Adds tests, observability, or security checks to important paths to reduce foreseeable failures.
domain-expertise.evidence: Tests or runtime signals demonstrate that key constraints are protected.

domain-expertise.text: Validates AI-generated or suggested work in proportion to its risk.
domain-expertise.evidence: Evidence includes tests, comparison cases, reference checks, or human approval.

team-influence.text: Aligns dependencies and acceptance with product, design, and partner teams to deliver a feature.
team-influence.evidence: Decisions, dependencies, and owners are clear; changes are shared promptly.

team-influence.text: Helps peers avoid repeat problems through reviews, documentation, or sharing.
team-influence.evidence: Others reuse the practice; quality issues or handoff costs decline.

team-influence.text: Resolves collaboration disagreements by clarifying facts and constraints and reaching an actionable decision.
team-influence.evidence: The disagreement ends with a decision, owner, and review point.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Changes the plan when evidence invalidates an assumption instead of defending the original approach.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Shows how new evidence changed priority or implementation.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Builds trust by keeping commitments, surfacing bad news early, and aligning expectations.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Partners can plan around updates and face fewer surprises.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Knows when AI can assist, when expert review is needed, and when to stop automation.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Identifies data, access, accuracy, or impact-scope risks.

stages.name: Senior Engineer
stages.summary: Independently shapes ambiguous problems and owns the user value, quality, and outcome of cross-functional work.

business-results.text: Turns an ambiguous request into a verifiable user or business outcome with baselines and guardrails.
business-results.evidence: The team can explain why, how success is measured, and when to stop or adjust.

business-results.text: Uses user evidence, market or operational constraints to align cross-functional teams on high-value work.
business-results.evidence: Priorities reflect opportunity cost and are revisited against outcomes.

business-results.text: Assesses contribution to outcomes and distinguishes causal evidence from correlation.
business-results.evidence: Explains metric definitions, observation window, guardrails, and attribution limits.

domain-expertise.text: Designs across component boundaries, balancing domain rules, system constraints, evolution cost, and reversibility.
domain-expertise.evidence: Proposal covers boundaries, trade-offs, migration/rollback, and failure paths.

domain-expertise.text: Validates the problem with users and product partners before choosing an implementation.
domain-expertise.evidence: Research, prototypes, experiments, or data narrow or invalidate an approach.

domain-expertise.text: Defines quality, security, and AI evaluation requirements for high-impact solutions.
domain-expertise.evidence: Shows evaluation cases, monitoring/escalation conditions, privacy/access controls, or human handoff.

team-influence.text: Aligns multiple teams on goals, dependencies, and decision rights without relying on reporting authority.
team-influence.evidence: Produces an accepted plan, commitments, and escalation path.

team-influence.text: Raises team-wide quality through review standards, shared components, or operating mechanisms.
team-influence.evidence: Rework, incidents, or duplicated implementations decline, not just documentation volume.

team-influence.text: Helps peers take on larger problems through delegation with clear boundaries and feedback.
team-influence.evidence: Others deliver independently and reliance on personal rescue declines.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Makes testable judgments under incomplete information and states confidence, risk, and disconfirming evidence.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Decision includes explicit assumptions and signals for reconsideration.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Understands partners’ goals and constraints and remains direct, respectful, and trustworthy through conflict.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Disagreements are discussable and commitments executable without avoiding hard issues.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Reviews outcomes and personal judgment to create learning that changes later behavior.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: A later project uses the changed mechanism and can explain its effect.

stages.name: Experienced Senior Engineer
stages.summary: On the senior individual-contributor path, shapes domain or multi-team outcomes, technical direction, and reusable mechanisms.

business-results.text: Translates domain-level business goals into sustainable product, technical, and operational outcomes.
business-results.evidence: Roadmap connects business measures, capability investment, and long-term cost.

business-results.text: Guides market, business-model, and long-term investment choices across opportunities.
business-results.evidence: Decision states opportunity cost, downside scenarios, and evidence thresholds for further investment.

business-results.text: Establishes cross-team outcome reviews that shape priorities and subsequent investment.
business-results.evidence: Review shares definitions and attribution limits, assigns actions, and changes resource choices.

domain-expertise.text: Sets evolvable domain architecture and professional standards while balancing product experience and engineering boundaries.
domain-expertise.evidence: Multiple teams adopt the approach and track quality, cost, and evolution outcomes.

domain-expertise.text: Builds quality and AI evaluation mechanisms so teams can compare approaches and detect regressions.
domain-expertise.evidence: Reusable baselines, production monitoring, and clear human-intervention/rollback conditions exist.

domain-expertise.text: Identifies cross-team complexity or technical debt and makes the overall system simpler and more reliable.
domain-expertise.evidence: Consumers repeat less work and incidents, change cost, or complexity decline.

team-influence.text: Aligns and enables multiple teams through clear direction and shared decisions rather than personal approval.
team-influence.evidence: Cross-team leads make aligned decisions independently.

team-influence.text: Develops new technical or product leaders and creates succession capacity.
team-influence.evidence: Multiple people can independently own critical areas.

team-influence.text: Improves team boundaries, collaboration, or decision mechanisms to remove recurring systemic blockers.
team-influence.evidence: Collaboration cycles or dependency risk improve sustainably and multiple teams adopt the mechanism.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Calibrates judgment on long-term uncertainty and knows when to invest, experiment, wait, or stop.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Across decisions, risk is calibrated and views update in time, not only explained after the fact.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Builds relationships across disciplines, locations, and interests where real disagreement is safe.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Partners share bad news early and engage in difficult trade-offs.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Updates judgments openly, incorporates outside evidence, and helps the organization revise its understanding.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Decision records preserve original assumptions and updates for later teams to reuse.

stages.name: Engineering Manager
stages.summary: Delivers business outcomes through the team rather than personal rescue, building talent, collaboration, and sustainable engineering quality.

business-results.text: Defines team goals, outcome measures, and quality guardrails with partners and recalibrates priorities.
business-results.evidence: The team explains outcomes and trade-offs and adjusts based on evidence.

business-results.text: Allocates capacity across delivery, reliability, talent growth, and technical investment.
business-results.evidence: Allocation reflects business risk and outcomes, with trade-offs recorded.

business-results.text: Owns team outcomes and explains how management decisions contributed and where attribution is limited.
business-results.evidence: Distinguishes team delivery, external conditions, and personal contribution without appropriating credit.

domain-expertise.text: Uses enough domain expertise to review critical product, technical, quality, and AI-risk decisions.
domain-expertise.evidence: Asks the right questions, involves appropriate experts, and owns the decision.

domain-expertise.text: Builds sustainable team practices for testing, release, incident response, and AI use.
domain-expertise.evidence: Quality and recovery are measurable without excessive manager approval.

domain-expertise.text: Enables product, design, and engineering to discover problems and validate outcomes end to end.
domain-expertise.evidence: The team tracks adoption and outcomes, not just on-time releases.

team-influence.text: Builds capabilities for team goals through hiring, feedback, coaching, and performance management.
team-influence.evidence: Role gaps and growth goals are clear; performance decisions use sustained evidence.

team-influence.text: Designs clear goals, ownership, delegation, and decision mechanisms that reduce recurring friction.
team-influence.evidence: Issues are resolved at the right level and members have decision space.

team-influence.text: Manages cross-team commitments, conflict, and escalation so the team can focus on key outcomes.
team-influence.evidence: Partners accept priorities and escalation paths; conflicts do not remain unresolved.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Makes people decisions from sustained, multi-source evidence while checking bias and uncertainty.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Can explain evidence, counterevidence, and follow-up observations.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Builds relationships where mistakes, risks, and disagreement can be discussed candidly while maintaining accountability.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Issues surface earlier and retrospectives use evidence.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Reviews whether management mechanisms produce intended outcomes and adjusts personal behavior.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Feedback and team signals lead to specific management changes and follow-up.

stages.name: Manager of Managers
stages.summary: Owns multi-team or organizational outcomes through managers, allocating resources and building long-term organizational capability.

business-results.text: Translates business direction into organizational outcomes, portfolio priorities, and adjustable investment plans.
business-results.evidence: Team goals form a coherent portfolio and outcomes/resources are revisited regularly.

business-results.text: Makes organization-level trade-offs across growth, efficiency, reliability, safety, and long-term capability.
business-results.evidence: Names downside scenarios, risk owners, and conditions for changing course.

business-results.text: Establishes consistent outcome measurement and review so leaders adjust direction using evidence.
business-results.evidence: Cross-team measures are interpretable; attribution limits and misses are transparent.

domain-expertise.text: Ensures clear ownership and controls for critical technical, product, AI, privacy, and security risks.
domain-expertise.evidence: Critical risks have decision owners, monitoring, review, and response mechanisms.

domain-expertise.text: Sets cross-team quality and operational standards proportionate to business risk.
domain-expertise.evidence: Standards reduce incidents or regressions without unnecessary process burden.

domain-expertise.text: Engages experts on long-term domain and technical choices and understands business, user, and organizational consequences.
domain-expertise.evidence: Can compare paths and reversibility without substituting for specialists on details.

team-influence.text: Hires, coaches, and evaluates managers and builds sustainable leadership succession.
team-influence.evidence: Managers independently own team results and grow the next layer of leaders.

team-influence.text: Adapts organizational boundaries, decision rights, and collaboration to business and architecture changes.
team-influence.evidence: Reduces structural dependencies and local optimization; ownership and resources match goals.

team-influence.text: Builds organization-wide mechanisms for strategic communication, conflict resolution, and decisions.
team-influence.evidence: Key trade-offs have clear decision owners and teams understand shared direction and limits.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Makes careful decisions under high uncertainty and competing interests, owning consequences and correction.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Decisions account for long-term risk, ethics, and counterevidence, not only short-term metrics.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Builds organizational trust and candor so information travels upward and bad news surfaces early.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Risks from different levels reach decisions and commitments remain transparent.

human-competitive-advantage.text: Turns reviews and external change into organizational capability renewal rather than one-off action items.
human-competitive-advantage.evidence: Practices evolve with evidence and learning transfers across teams.
